newsitem.title: UK: Med refiners mull run cuts as margins dip into red.
newsitem.headline: Med refiners mull run cuts as margins dip into red.

text.p: Mediterranean refiners were considering cutting back crude runs on Tuesday after margins fell below break-even levels at simple processing units.
The margin for running Russian Urals through a hydroskimming refinery averaged minus 35 cents a barrel on Monday, and slipped further on Tuesday as benchmark Brent made further gains.
"These are the worst margins in the last few months," said an Italian refiner. "We are looking at cuts -- there is a good chance that we will cut runs."

Differentials for Urals in the Mediterranean have been climbing steadily in recent weeks, from a low of around Dated Brent minus $1.40 at the beginning of June to a traded high of Dated Brent minus 65 cents on Monday.
Most first half July Urals was already committed, and other sour grades were also scarce, with a third decade Syrian Light snapped up at 10 cents above the official selling price for July on Friday.
But further gains may be capped, with buyers only with very prompt requirements expected to venture into the market.
"Refiners are scared of these new numbers...As soon as they have covered their minimum requirements they will cut back runs," said a trader.
Sour markets have been buoyed in recent weeks by the absence of Iraqi crude. Sales under the first six-month term of the United Nations oil-for-food agreement dried up in late May.
The market consensus is that exports under the second term are unlikely before August, in line with recent comments made by Iraqi envoy Abdul Amir al-Anbari.
"If you can possibly wait for (Iraqi) Kirkuk, then you will," said a local refiner.
